title: CogniDir: Combating Cognitive Malicious Comments via Adaptive Distributional Learning for Robust Fake News Detection
tldr: LLM-generated adversarial comments exploit fact distortion, logical confusion, and emotional manipulation to break comment-aware fake news detectors. CogniDir synthesizes mechanism-labeled attacks and reallocates training with InfoDirichlet Resampling. Robust F1 improves by up to +17.9% on Weibo20, where Macro-F1 reaches 0.947.
abstract: CogniDir reformulates robust fake news detection as adaptive distributional learning. It builds mechanism-specific adversarial comments covering fact distortion, logical confusion, and emotional manipulation, then maps group-wise vulnerability to sampling proportions through a Dirichlet-mean parameterization. The resulting allocation smoothly shifts training exposure toward the most brittle attack mechanisms. Across Weibo16, Weibo20, and RumourEval-19, CogniDir improves F1 by up to 17.9% and reduces mean attack success rate by 45%.

methodOverview: CogniDir works in three stages: mechanism-specific malicious comment generation, InfoDirichlet Resampling that updates the training mixture from group vulnerability after each epoch, and robust evaluation under mixed adversarial comments. The mixture uses the Dirichlet mean, a smooth closed-form allocation that tracks the weakest attack group.
contributions: A cognitive-grounded synthesis pipeline that produces mechanism-labeled comments for fact distortion, logical confusion, and emotional manipulation.
InfoDirichlet Resampling, which turns group-wise vulnerability into an adaptive training mixture through the Dirichlet mean.
Strong robustness on Weibo16, Weibo20, and RumourEval-19, with up to +17.9% F1 and a 45% reduction in mean ASR.
mainResults: On Weibo16, CogniDir keeps F1 near 0.94 across attack categories, while prior detectors drop sharply under diverse malicious comments.
Robust F1 improves by +9.0% on Weibo16, +17.9% on Weibo20 (Macro-F1 0.947), and +14.5% on RumourEval-19 over the strongest baselines.
Adaptive training reduces mean ASR by 45%, down to 0.116, across attack types and comment counts.
Malicious-comment generation, vulnerability scoring, and Dirichlet expectation allocation each contribute to the final robustness.
priorWorkDiff: CogniDir keeps a separate training budget for each attack mechanism and updates that budget from feedback. InfoDirichlet Resampling uses the Dirichlet mean to give the weakest group more exposure at the next epoch, so robustness improves together across fact distortion, logical confusion, and emotional manipulation.

attackCategories.name: Fact Distortion
attackCategories.description: Injects unverified or misleading factual details to create false credibility and encourage dissemination.

attackCategories.name: Logical Confusion
attackCategories.description: Exploits causal fallacies and contradictory reasoning to undermine the detector's verification boundaries.

attackCategories.name: Emotional Manipulation
attackCategories.description: Uses affective framing and social pressure to shift attention away from veracity signals in the news–comment pair.

findings.title: Mechanism-specific attacks
findings.text: Fact distortion, logical confusion, and emotional manipulation are generated and evaluated as distinct comment attacks, exposing different weaknesses in comment-aware detectors.

findings.title: Adaptive training mixture
findings.text: InfoDirichlet Resampling converts vulnerability scores into the next epoch mixture through the Dirichlet mean, shifting data toward the attack group that is currently weakest.

findings.title: Code
findings.text: Training, evaluation, and InfoDirichlet Resampling are available at https://github.com/cheslyn0712/CogniDir.

faqs.q: How do LLM-generated adversarial comments affect fake news detectors?
faqs.a: Comments built from fact distortion, logical confusion, and emotional manipulation substantially lower the F1 of comment-aware detectors. On Weibo16, CogniDir holds F1 near 0.94 across these attack categories.

faqs.q: Why does vulnerability differ across manipulation mechanisms?
faqs.a: Each mechanism stresses a different part of the news-comment signal. CogniDir measures that difference during training and gives the weaker mechanism a larger share of the next epoch.

faqs.q: How does CogniDir adapt the adversarial training mixture?
faqs.a: After each epoch it scores every attack group, sets a positive Dirichlet parameter from that score, and uses the Dirichlet mean as the next sampling proportion. The mixture therefore follows the latest vulnerability feedback.
CogniDir is evaluated on Weibo16, Weibo20, and RumourEval-19, covering Chinese and English comment-based fake news detection under multiple attack types and comment counts.

faqs.q: What does the Dirichlet allocation provide?
faqs.a: The Dirichlet mean gives a smooth, closed-form training mixture. As vulnerability scores change, exposure moves toward the brittle attack group while every group keeps a positive share.
